title: Portobello and Black Pepper Pan Sauce
description: Finely chopped portobello caps brown against the skillet and give this smooth mushroom reduction a savory backbone.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh portobello mushroom caps
ingredients.note: Weigh after trimming and mince finely.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Heat {oil} in the HexClad over medium heat. Spread {caps} across the pan and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid evaporates and the edges turn brown.

steps.title: Lift the browned bits
steps.text: Sprinkle {pepper} over the mushrooms, then add a splash of {broth}. Scrape the skillet with a silicone spatula until the browned bits dissolve.

steps.title: Reduce the broth
steps.text: Pour in the remaining broth and {aminos}. Simmer uncovered for 6–8 minutes until the mushrooms are soft.

steps.title: Blend the pan sauce
steps.text: Puree the mushrooms with their liquid until smooth. Press the puree through a fine sieve into the skillet.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 1/2 cups total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon over braised chuck, turkey cutlets or soft potato mash. Divide the remaining sauce into measured portions for later meals.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Brown the mushrooms and deglaze the pan up to a day ahead. Chill the base and finish when needed. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The smooth mushroom base freezes well for up to 2 months. Whisk once it bubbles again. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses finely ground black pepper. For a gentler Option B, omit it and add a pinch of dried thyme while reducing the broth. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 26 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 2.4 g total carbohydrate, 1.6 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 21 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
